patient_information: A 2-month-old baby girl, born at term, presented to a paediatric intensive care unit in Vientiane, Laos; her mother is a 24-year-old rice farmer.
chief_complaint: The patient presented with 3 days of irritability, dyspnoea, and grunting.
history_of_present_illness: The infant suddenly became unwell 3 days prior to presentation, but was neither feverish nor coughing, and had been very well until then.
exposure_and_epidemiology: The patient is from Vientiane, Laos, and was exclusively breastfed by her mother, a rice farmer who practiced food avoidance (avoiding beef, pork, vegetables, and fruits) postpartum, a common tradition in lowland Lao culture.
vitals: Temperature was 37.0°C (98.6°F), pulse 140 bpm, and respiratory rate 40 breath cycles per minute; blood pressure was not taken.
physical_exam: The infant was irritable, crying, grunting, dyspnoeic, and had central cyanosis, hepatomegaly, and oedematous extremities, with a clear chest and no heart murmurs, indicating signs of heart failure and poor breastfeeding.
labs_and_diagnostics: Blood samples taken from both the child and mother showed they were thiamine-deficient.
differential_diagnosis: Initial differential diagnoses included congenital heart disease, respiratory diseases (e.g., bronchopneumonia, bronchiolitis, laryngitis), meningitis, and infantile beriberi; infantile beriberi was considered the most likely diagnosis.
management_and_clinical_course: Intravenous thiamine (50 mg) was immediately administered, leading to a quick and dramatic response within 30-60 minutes; six hours later the baby was able to breastfeed normally and was discharged the following day, while the mother received oral thiamine supplementation and advice on a well-balanced, thiamine-rich diet.
